board.note: Elected October 14, 2026 for calendar 2027. Dill is also Secretary. Two seats changed hands mid-2026: Ardent's Marty Bonick, the 2026 chair-elect, left Ardent on June 2 and his successor Dave Caspers took the seat. ScionHealth's Rob Jay moved to executive chairman on June 10 and new CEO Doug Shirley took his.

lobbying.narrative: FAH reported $3.57 million of federal lobbying in 2025, its highest year since 2019, and $1.91 million through the third quarter of 2026. Four in-house lobbyists are registered, including the CEO. Five outside firms are on retainer in 2026. Three others were dropped at the turn of the year, and BGR Government Affairs was added in January. The figures are FAH's own quarterly Senate filings, which already include what it pays the firms.

revolvingDoor.narrative: At least 27 people lobbying for FAH in 2026, in-house or at its retained firms, came from Congress or the White House. The CEO came from a Democratic whip's office. The head of government relations ran a Senate HELP health subcommittee before a decade at Merck. The retained firms supply former staff to Majority Leader McConnell, Whip Cornyn, Sen. Cassidy, Sen. Murray, Speaker Pelosi and the Senate Finance Committee. Names and prior posts come from the covered-position fields on Senate lobbying filings and the firms' own bios.

pahcf.narrative: The Partnership for America's Health Care Future is the dark-money coalition FAH founded with the insurers' and drugmakers' lobbies in June 2018. Its purpose: stop Medicare for All and a public option. It is a 501(c)(4), so its donors are secret. Its Form 990s show $99.6 million spent from 2018 through 2024, with $55.4 million raised in 2019 alone. Chip Kahn, then FAH's CEO, was its secretary and then its president through 2024. It is still posting statements in November 2026, now against a public option, and its members page is blank.

pac.name: FEDPAC
pac.narrative: FEDPAC is FAH's federal political action committee, registered in 1976 and filing monthly. It raised $754,000 in the 2025-26 cycle through October 14, 2026, nearly all from individuals, and gave $825,000 to candidates and committees. Candidate money this cycle ran 53% Republican and 47% Democratic; the four national party committees got $115,000 between them, split evenly. In 2023-24 it leaned slightly Democratic. Its treasurer is FAH's head of government relations, Rebecca Heilig Lira.

developments.text: Statement after the House Ways and Means hearing on health systems: there is no replacement for a local hospital when you need it most.
Elizabeth Schwartz hired from Merck as Senior Vice President and Head of Government Relations.
FAH rebuts a Families USA post on corporate hospital pricing as not a serious analysis of affordability.
Statement welcoming the No Surprises Act IDR operations final rule.
Board change: 2026 chair-elect Marty Bonick steps down at Ardent; Dave Caspers becomes CEO and later takes the FAH seat.
Board change: ScionHealth names Doug Shirley CEO; Rob Jay moves to executive chairman and off the FAH board.
Statement for the House Energy and Commerce transparency hearing: patients' costs are dictated primarily by insurers' benefit design.

FAH joins AHA, the Children's Hospital Association and AAMC on a Fifth Circuit amicus brief backing Texas. The case concerns CMS's reading of the Medicaid hold-harmless rules for state hospital taxes.
Statement on the House subcommittee price transparency markup: duplicative and impractical hospital reporting requirements will not help patients.
Statement on the CY2027 outpatient proposed rule objecting to accelerated 340B recoupment.
Statement on the Ways and Means markup praising Medicare Advantage transparency measures.
Statement on the Energy and Commerce markup: transparency works when it produces meaningful information for patients, not just more data.
Statement on the FY2027 inpatient final rule: adequate Medicare payments become even more critical as uncompensated care grows.
CY2027 outpatient comment letter: supports the 340B cut to acquisition cost; opposes the imaging site-neutral cut and the faster recoupment.
Statement on CMS Marketplace anti-fraud actions: Americans are being priced out of health insurance and losing coverage.
Paul Eiting hired from the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association as Vice President, Policy.
2027 board elected: Hazen chair, Sutaria chair-elect, Dill past chair and secretary, Tarr treasurer; directors Caspers, Hammons, Miller, Reddy, Shirley.
Q3 2026 lobbying report: $760,000, the highest quarter of 2026; four in-house lobbyists.
PAHCF, the coalition FAH co-founded, issues a post-election statement that Medicare for All and the public option are not the answer.
CMS finalizes the CY2027 outpatient rule over FAH's objections on imaging site-neutral payment and the 2% recoupment.

bottomLine: The Federation of American Hospitals is nine chief executives and $3.6 million a year in lobbying. Beside it sits a dark-money coalition that has spent $99.6 million since 2018. Its board runs more than 700 hospitals and carries more than $3 billion in federal fraud settlements. In 2025 and 2026 it fought the two reforms that matter most to an independent physician: site-neutral payment and the right to own a hospital. Chip Kahn said the physician-owned hospital ban would not exist without the Federation. Sixteen years in, four repeal bills sit in committee and the Federation's new CEO came from the whip's office.
